summary: Klamath Indian Agency lookout site about three miles southeast of the Agency; the 1927 report describes use on smoky and hazy days, and the blog says it was dropped when Agency Butte was set up.

events.note: Annual forestry report: two primary lookouts and one secondary lookout on the butte, elevation 4,700 feet, used only in smoky and hazy weather

evidence.supports: Listed as an emergency lookout in 1925
evidence.quote: 1925: The butte was listed as an emergency lookout.

evidence.supports: Butte about three miles southeast of the Agency
evidence.quote: located about three miles southeast of the Agency

evidence.supports: Two main and one secondary lookout on the butte, per the 1927 report
evidence.quote: two primary lookouts and one secondary lookout located on Steiger Butte

evidence.supports: Used only in smoky and hazy weather, when primary lookouts could not see the western reservation
evidence.quote: Steiger Butte is used only in smoky and hazy weather when the primary lookouts are unable to see the western part of the reservation.

evidence.supports: Managing agency is the Klamath Indian Agency
Construction dated only to the 1920s; structures unknown
Used on smoky days; discontinued when Agency Butte was established
evidence.quote: Comments: Used on smokey days, was discontinued when Agency Butte was established.

evidence.supports: Agency Butte first lookout was a tree with a crow's nest, constructed 1930
The Agency Butte tree lookout came first; the tower followed later that year
evidence.quote: The Klamath Agency built the tree lookout, later that same year the Crater National Forest erected the tower

notes_for_editor: Two sources only. The Forest Lookouts page supplies the 1925 and 1927 facts. The Klamath County blog supplies the managing agency, the 1920s construction date and the link to Agency Butte; it gives no removal date and no description of the structures, so the record cannot say what was built. The blog gives no date for Steiger's discontinuation; the 1930 year belongs to the Agency Butte entry, so the 1930 'abandoned' event was removed from this record. Ownership and access today are not in either source. The brief's Klamath County and 34S-7E-29 location agree with both sources.
